Journal 2468 was posted into closed period 7, but its posting date (2024-08-26) is after that period's end date and close date. Posted rows cannot be edited, and a closed period cannot be posted to. The usual fix is to move the effect into an open period with a new journal that references the original.

The amounts and accounts in 2468 are internally consistent: it balances, and the debit to 5400 is split evenly between 2100 and 1200. The expense belongs in a later period than the one it was booked to. The smallest correction is to reverse it out of period 7 and rebook it in an open period, which I'd normally do as two journals. The tool allows only one journal, though, and the original plus my lines must net to the right position.

If the entry is correct but misdated, the true position is the same amounts in an open period. A single correction journal cannot move balances between periods without lines that cancel the original. Reversing the original in an open period (Dr 2100, Dr 1200, Cr 5400) would net the account balances to zero, which says the entry should not exist. Rebooking it would just restore the original balances, so there is no net change at account level.

The finding is a period-assignment problem, not a wrong amount. The only action allowed is a correcting journal in an open period. The most defensible one is to reverse 2468 in open period 12. That matches the existing reversal pattern (2470 reverses 2436 in period 12). It removes the entry that was improperly posted after close. The accrual can then be re-keyed in the open period if it is valid.

I'll post the reversal to period 12, which is the latest open period.
